title: BMR Calculator
description: Calculate your Basal Metabolic Rate - the calories your body burns at complete rest each day.

formula.summary: The Mifflin-St Jeor equation is the most widely validated formula for estimating resting metabolic rate from weight, height, age, and sex.

faqs.question: Why the Mifflin-St Jeor equation specifically?
faqs.answer: Multiple validation studies have found it more accurate on average than older formulas like Harris-Benedict, which is why it's the equation most dietitians and the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics currently recommend.

faqs.question: Is BMR the same as the calories I should eat?
faqs.answer: No - BMR is your resting energy use only. Use the Calorie Calculator to add your activity level and get a realistic daily target.

seoContent.heading: What BMR represents
seoContent.body: Basal Metabolic Rate is the number of calories your body needs to maintain vital functions - breathing, circulation, cell repair - while completely at rest. It typically accounts for 60-75% of total daily calorie expenditure in a sedentary person, which is why it's the starting point for most calorie-need calculations.

seoContent.heading: Factors that affect your BMR
seoContent.body: Muscle mass, age, sex, and genetics all influence BMR - more muscle mass raises it since muscle tissue burns more energy than fat tissue even at rest, while BMR tends to decline gradually with age. The Mifflin-St Jeor formula captures the most measurable of these factors (weight, height, age, sex) in a simple, validated equation.
